# Realm Object Model — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Realm Object Model. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-24 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] In the inspected Swift Object implementation, @Persisted marks stored properties; properties without that wrapper are ignored when using this declaration style. @Persisted(primaryKey: true) declares the primary key, whose values enforce uniqueness and receive an automatic index. (low confidence) — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Realm models persisted data with typed classes and properties: Swift model classes subclass Object, while Java model classes subclass RealmObject and add fields to be persisted. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] An embedded Realm object has exactly one parent and no primary key. It is created through its parent rather than added as an independent top-level object. Deleting its parent deletes the embedded object; Swift also deletes it when the parent removes its owning link. (high confidence) — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/EmbeddedObject.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-dotnet/discussions/2594

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Realm object models support relationships through references to other model objects and typed collections. The inspected Swift implementation also exposes LinkingObjects for inverse links, alongside List, MutableSet, and Map collections. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] A newly instantiated Swift Realm object can be unmanaged. Adding it to a Realm makes it managed; subsequent persisted mutations must occur inside a write transaction. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/device-sdks/sdk/swift/crud/update.md — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://realm.netlify.app/docs/swift/latest/
- [statement] In Swift and Java, managed objects and query results are live: Swift Results is an auto-updating container returned from object queries, and Java RealmResults are live views that update after a transaction is committed on a Looper thread. A managed Java object is a wrapper around the data in the underlying Realm file and, on Looper threads, is live-updated; a change listener can be registered to be notified of changes. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Results.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmResults.java ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java ; https://koenig-assets.raywenderlich.com/32960966-realm-with-swiftui-tutorial-getting-started?page=1 — https://koenig-assets.raywenderlich.com/32960966-realm-with-swiftui-tutorial-getting-started?page=1 · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] Embedded objects express exclusive ownership: a single parent owns the embedded object, and it is automatically deleted when the parent is deleted or when the parent no longer points at it. The Swift implementation allows only one parent to link to an embedded object and throws an exception when linking to an existing managed embedded object. The .NET changelog records that linking to an already-managed embedded object historically threw an exception, though setting a property to the same embedded object it already holds is now a no-op. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/EmbeddedObject.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-dotnet/main/CHANGELOG.md — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/EmbeddedObject.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://realm.github.io/realm-dotnet/CHANGELOG.html
- [statement] Swift frozen objects are immutable snapshots that do not advance with subsequent writes and can be read across threads. Live objects have thread or actor confinement requirements, so a stored object reference is not automatically safe to pass between execution contexts. (high confidence) — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/discussions/7685
- [statement] Realm Kotlin's 0.4.0 release notes, dated 2021-07-13, explicitly changed its architecture from thread-confined live objects to frozen objects. Results outside write transactions became frozen, updates arrived through Flows, and MutableRealm.findLatest supplied a mutable live version inside a write transaction. (low confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-kotlin/main/CHANGELOG.md — https://github.com/realm/realm-kotlin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- [statement] Retaining frozen objects while continuing to write can pin old database versions and increase file size. Swift source documentation and the Kotlin changelog both warn about this retention cost; frozen references should not be treated as cost-free long-lived value copies. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-kotlin/main/CHANGELOG.md — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-kotlin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- [statement] A March 2022 .NET issue reports invalidated collection access with nested Xamarin collection views and background updates. Its reduced example produces RealmInvalidObjectException after collection deletion or Realm closure; the reporter explicitly says that example does not reproduce the separate Access to invalidated Collection object exception. (low confidence) — https://github.com/realm/realm-dotnet/issues/2888
- [statement] Realm model declarations define persisted fields in application code. Swift uses Object subclasses with @Persisted properties; the Android Java tutorial uses RealmObject subclasses with annotations such as @Required and @PrimaryKey. These SDK syntaxes should not be treated as interchangeable. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/ — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] Realm models represent relationships through object-valued properties and typed collections. Swift supports links to Object subclasses and List collections; the Java tutorial demonstrates RealmObject and RealmList fields for relationships. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/examples/introExample/src/main/java/io/realm/examples/intro/model/Person.java — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] In Swift, constructing an Object produces an unmanaged instance; Realm.add makes it managed. Its realm property is nil while unmanaged. Java also distinguishes managed proxy objects from unmanaged model instances. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-java/blob/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java
- [statement] Primary keys provide object identity and enforce uniqueness within a model type. Swift documents that primary key properties enforce uniqueness and that indexes are created automatically for them, and supports @Persisted(primaryKey: true); the Java example demonstrates an annotated @PrimaryKey field that identifies a specific object when writes update existing objects. Supported key types depend on the SDK (Swift: String, Int, ObjectId, UUID). Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/examples/introExample/src/main/java/io/realm/examples/intro/model/Person.java — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] Live managed objects have thread or execution-context restrictions. Swift and Java expose frozen immutable snapshots that can be read across threads; these snapshots do not behave as mutable, automatically advancing live objects. Retaining old frozen versions while writing can increase the Realm file size. (high confidence) Sources: https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-java/blob/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java
- [statement] Managed Realm objects support change observation, but live does not mean synchronous cross-thread notification. Swift delivers changes after the managing Realm advances to the relevant version, and a blocked run loop can delay or coalesce callbacks. (high confidence) — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/EmbeddedObject.swift
- [statement] Deleting a managed object invalidates its accessors. Swift exposes isInvalidated and Java exposes isValid; applications must check object validity before accessing a retained reference after deletion. (high confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-swift/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/realm/realm-java/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java — https://github.com/realm/realm-swift/blob/master/RealmSwift/Object.swift · keywords: Realm Object Model · also: https://github.com/realm/realm-java/blob/master/realm/realm-library/src/main/java/io/realm/RealmObject.java
- [statement] The Android tutorial requires create, update, and delete operations on persisted Realm data to run inside write transactions. Committing persists the transaction; cancelling discards its changes. (low confidence) — https://auth0.com/blog/integrating-realm-database-in-an-android-application/
- [statement] In a hands-on Android forensic example published November 20, 2019, the researcher recovered name and age values from default.realm and inspected them with Realm Studio. This establishes a concrete local persistence example, not a guarantee about every application file location or format version. (low confidence) — https://abrignoni.blogspot.com/2019/11/realm-database-storage-primer-for.html
